truth: a servlet whose write path is a thin adapter over its dispatch class (types/dashboard.md DUX1) takes the
CSRF token check from that class (retro kit-p1-security-guards Δ4). The dispatch class is a type the servlet
names in code, declared by a file of the scanned tree in the servlet's own directory (the DUX1 route/
package); a verifyCsrfToken( call or a CsrfProtectedFilter in it counts, so neither servlet below WARNs.
-- args --
@DIR@/m
-- want --
exit 0
-- stderr --
-- m/BPanelServlet.java --
public class BPanelServlet extends BWebServlet {
  void doPost(WebOp op) {
    if (!PanelDispatch.accept(op)) return;
    if (!target.getPermissions(op).hasOperatorWrite()) return;
    target.set(p, v, op);
  }
}
-- m/PanelDispatch.java --
final class PanelDispatch {
  static boolean accept(WebOp op) {
    CsrfUtil.verifyCsrfToken(op.getRequest());
    return true;
  }
}
-- m/BFilterServlet.java --
public class BFilterServlet extends BWebServlet {
  void doPost(WebOp op) {
    if (!FilterDispatch.accept(op)) return;
    if (!target.getPermissions(op).hasOperatorWrite()) return;
    target.set(p, v, op);
  }
}
-- m/FilterDispatch.java --
final class FilterDispatch {
  static boolean accept(WebOp op) {
    CsrfProtectedFilter guard = new CsrfProtectedFilter();
    return true;
  }
}
